samasa.vigraha: pramāṇaṃ ca viparyayaś ca vikalpaś ca nidrā ca smṛtiś ca

analysis.note: An itaretara-dvandva enumerating five types; the compound takes the feminine i-stem inflection of the final member smṛti. Semantically it continues the preceding topic, vṛttayaḥ, ‘modifications’.

verification.detail: compound stem pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛti as Stri/Prathama/Bahu: pass; relation dvandva: unsupported (logged)

justifications.decision: The long compound is not construed as a dependent tatpuruṣa such as ‘memory of sleep ...’, but as an itaretara-dvandva naming five parallel items; the nominative plural ending supplies the predication from the preceding sūtra, ‘[the modifications] are ...’.
options_considered: tatpuruṣa chain with smṛti as head
justifications.chosen: A co-ordinate dvandva list: pramāṇa, viparyaya, vikalpa, nidrā, and smṛti.

justifications.decision: Although pramāṇa can mean ‘measure’ lexically, the commentary immediately identifies pramāṇas as perception, inference, and āgama, showing the epistemological Yoga sense.
options_considered: valid cognition / means of valid knowledge
justifications.chosen: pramāṇa is rendered as ‘valid cognition’ / ‘means of valid knowledge’, not merely ‘measure’.

evidence.translation: Perception, inference, and authoritative testimony are the pramāṇas.

justifications.decision: The supplied commentary on this unit does not gloss these four terms; the renderings therefore rest on grammar, Yoga context, and ordinary lexical values rather than on an explicit bhāṣya line here.
options_considered: vikalpa as option/alternative vs. conceptual construction
justifications.chosen: viparyaya, vikalpa, nidrā, and smṛti are translated as ‘error’, ‘conceptual construction’, ‘sleep’, and ‘memory’.

translation: Valid cognition (pramāṇa), error (viparyaya), conceptual construction (vikalpa), sleep (nidrā), and memory (smṛti) [are the five modifications].
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render pramāṇa as the ordinary ‘measure’ or ‘standard’; the bhāṣya line identifies it instead with the epistemic set perception, inference, and āgama.
It might misread the single long compound as a dependent chain headed by smṛti, whereas the form is a co-ordinate dvandva enumeration of the five vṛttis.
It might omit the syntactic carry-over from the preceding sūtra and so miss that these are the five mental modifications being listed.
open_questions: Only pramāṇa is glossed in the supplied commentary line; the other four technical renderings are not directly confirmed by this excerpt.
